algorithm: Constant-velocity Kalman prediction/correction with global Hungarian one-to-one assignment in map coordinates

output.id: Positive int16, 1..32767; skip occupied IDs when wrapping; expire after two seconds without a real observation
output.vx_vy: Absolute map x/y velocity, metres per second; initialize to zero until at least two observations spanning 0.2 seconds
output.heading: normalize_degrees(atan2(vx, vy) * 180 / pi), north zero, clockwise, [0,360)
output.zero_velocity_heading: Hold previous valid course; new track falls back to normalized ego heading minus local marker yaw in degrees
output.geometry: Published x/y/dx/dy remain latest real observations; predicted position is used only for association; lane type uses independent world corners
output.missing_observations: Keep last constant-velocity estimate, lower weighted confidence, never feed predicted targets into raw history

confidence: Preserve two-second exponentially weighted occurrence ratio including empty frames, grouped by tracker ID; retain original geometry-only filter as a compatibility API
transaction: Update a tracker copy; commit only after successful temporal filtering, lane classification and publication validation. Duplicate timestamps restore pre-frame motion state, preserve birth IDs from old detections, and keep the ID allocator progressing.

tracker.transport: stubs generated from actual ROS messages

coverage: Cardinal/diagonal heading, constant velocity, first observations, jitter, stopping and identities across multiple confidence windows
Crossing targets, changing array order, missing detections, predicted reacquisition and outlier isolation
Hungarian assignments versus exhaustive minimum-cost search on 300 deterministic random matrices
ID wrap, reset, exact expiry, duplicate timestamps, reordered/deleted/new births, motion rollback after failed callbacks
Ego translation/rotation compensation; course independent of box geometry and preserved 20 percent lane threshold
Nonuniform sample times and float32 large-map coordinates, ID-keyed confidence, duplicate-ID rejection and existing publication safety regressions
limitations: ROS message/transport stubs with real message definitions and existing real HDMap SDK; no ROS1 transport, Orin build or vehicle test
Receipt timestamps and current localization retain upstream latency/alignment errors; model/noise/deadband defaults need vehicle calibration
Existing float32 positions have approximately 0.25 m spacing at 4 million m map coordinates, causing short-term velocity quantization noise
Position and size alone cannot guarantee identities under complete overlap or long occlusion; IDs do not survive process restart
Benchmark covers tracker state copy, association, prediction and correction on this host, not the complete ROS callback
